Title: Runtime row singularity and DB uniqueness hardening
Purpose: Bring the runtime schema in line with service assumptions by enforcing singular step runs and singular run assignments directly in the database, including null-safe uniqueness for step-scoped versus run-scoped assignments.
Deliverables: A unique runtime invariant for one `ProcessStepRun` per `(ProcessRunId, StepDefinitionId)`.
A unique runtime invariant for one `ProcessRunAssignment` per `(ProcessRunId, RoleRequirementId)` at run scope and per `(ProcessRunId, RoleRequirementId, StepDefinitionId)` at step scope.
Friendly service-boundary handling for uniqueness conflicts where concurrency races can still occur.
Fresh integration tests proving duplicate runtime rows are rejected and concurrent assignment resolution cannot create duplicate rows silently.
ReviewQuestions: Can the DB still accept two step runs for the same run and step definition?
Can the DB still accept duplicate run assignments for the same logical scope when `StepDefinitionId` is null or non-null?
Do the runtime services still contain any `FirstOrDefault` or dictionary assumptions that are stronger than the schema guarantees?
CorrectiveOnFailure: If runtime singularity still depends only on service discipline or nullable non-unique indexes, stop and open the runtime-uniqueness corrective playbook.
